summary: Compute investment can be a weak process signal for allocating review attention, especially when it records search and verification. It is not proof of correctness and is meaningful only after task-normalized, outcome-based calibration.

points.text: Normalize by task class, difficulty proxy, model and revision, workflow, cache use, tool calls, hardware, and pricing date. Tokens or dollars across unlike tasks and providers are not comparable.

Separate generation, search, repair, independent evaluation, and failed attempts. Ten retries after the same failure have a different quality implication from ten diverse candidates checked by an external oracle.
Calibrate the fingerprint against held-out tests, defect escape, reviewer findings, rework, and rollback rates. If it does not improve review triage beyond those signals, remove it.
Use the signal to increase or decrease scrutiny within bounded bands, never to waive mandatory checks or rank contributors by spend.
